deep.reconstruction:
PROBLEM (title): find spherical right triangles in which every side and angle has rational sine and cosine. This is equivalent to every half-angle tangent being rational. Notation: legs p, q; hypotenuse r; angle P opposite p; angle Q opposite q; right angle opposite r. The page continues on the next one, which works the example (6,1),(5,2) and uses it for a rational pentagramma mirificum.

(1) PARAMETRIZATION. Gauss sets P = 90° + 2φ − 2φ' and Q = 2φ + 2φ'. Equivalently ½Q = φ + φ' and ½(90° − P) = φ' − φ. [My remark: 4φ = P + Q − 90° is the spherical excess E, and 4φ' = Q − P + 90°.]
He states three formulas:
- tan²(½p) = tan2φ / tan2φ'
- tan²(½q) = tan2φ · tan2φ'
- tan²(½r) = sin4φ / sin4φ'
[My derivation, from Napier's rules cos r = cot P cot Q, cos p = cos P / sin Q, cos q = cos Q / sin P:]
- tan²(½r) = (1 − cos r)/(1 + cos r) = −cos(P+Q)/cos(P−Q) = sin4φ / sin4φ'.
- tan²(½p) = (sin Q − cos P)/(sin Q + cos P). Here sin Q = sin(2φ+2φ') and −cos P = sin(2φ−2φ'), so the quotient is sin2φ cos2φ' / (cos2φ sin2φ').
- tan²(½q) = (sin P − cos Q)/(sin P + cos Q). Here sin P = cos(2φ−2φ'), so the quotient is tan2φ tan2φ'.

(2) RATIONALIZATION. Put a = u cosφ, b = u sinφ, a' = u' cosφ', b' = u' sinφ', with a, b, a', b' integers, so tanφ = b/a and u² = a² + b².
- Then tan2φ = 2ab/(a² − b²) and u⁴ sin4φ = 4ab(a² − b²).
- So everything is rational as soon as ab(a² − b²) and a'b'(a'² − b'²) are in the ratio of two squares.
- Gauss writes this as ab(a−b)(a+b) = k m² and a'b'(a'−b')(a'+b') = k m'². The prose writes (b−a); it is a sign convention.
- ab(a² − b²) is the area of the Pythagorean triangle (2ab, a² − b², a² + b²). So the condition is: two Pythagorean triangles whose areas have the same squarefree part k, i.e. the same congruent number. [Modern: two rational points x = a/b, x' = a'/b' on the same quadratic twist k y² = x³ − x of the congruent-number curve.]

(3) RESULTING FORMULAS (all verified by me):
- tan½r = m(a'² + b'²) / (m'(a² + b²))
- tan½p = m'ab/(m a'b') = m(a'² − b'²)/(m'(a² − b²)) = ab(a'² − b'²)/(k m m')
- tan½q = 2aba'b'/(k m m') = 2m'ab/(m(a'² − b'²)) = 2m a'b'/(m'(a² − b²))
- tan½(90° − P) = tan(φ' − φ) = (ab' − ba')/(aa' + bb')
- tan½Q = tan(φ + φ') = (ab' + ba')/(aa' − bb')
Check with the next page's example (a,b,a',b') = (6,1,5,2), k = 210, m = m' = 1. This gives 29/37, 3/5, 4/7, 7/32, 17/28. Then cos p cos q = (8/17)(33/65) = 264/1105 = cos r.

(4) TABLES OF SOLUTIONS (b, a, k), pairs sharing k:
- k = 6: (1,2), (24,25)
- k = 21: (1,7), (3,4)
- k = 210: (1,6), (2,5), (7,8)
- k = 330: (5,6), (3,8)
- k = 546: (6,7), (13,14), (7,32)
- Right column: (2,9),(7,18) k=154; (1,74),(73,74) k=3·73·74; (1,14),(13,?) k=2730; (8,17),(8,9) k=34; (4,9),(4,121) k=65; (16,17),(16,33) k=561; (2,17),(15,34) k=9690; (8,19),(11,38) k=1254; (8,33),(8,41) k=2706; (5,54),(27,32) k=1770; (8,9),(32,49) k=34.

GENERAL RULE ('allgemein'): from (g,h), the pair (4gh(h² − g²), (g² + h²)²) has the same k.
- Reason: with X = (h² − g²)² and Y = 4g²h², (X + Y)² − 4XY = (X − Y)².
- So A² − B² = ((h² − g²)² − 4g²h²)² is a perfect square.
- Examples on the page: (2,3) → (120,169) and (1,4) → (240,289); also (1,2) → (24,25) in the main table.
- This is the classical Fermat/Euler 'new triangle with the same area' construction, i.e. doubling on the congruent-number curve.

(5) PENTAGON. 'Seiten des Fünfecks dessen 10 Diagonalen 90°' refers to the self-polar spherical pentagon (pentagramma mirificum).
- Its consecutive parts are r, 90 − p, P, Q, 90 − q, i.e. Napier's circular parts.
- The opposite angles are 180 − r, 90 + p, 180 − P, 180 − Q, 90 + q.
- A rational right triangle therefore yields a pentagramma mirificum with rational sines and cosines; this is carried out on the next page with stereographic coordinates.
errors: The prose condition ab(b−a)(b+a) and the formula ab(a−b)(b+a) differ in sign. This is harmless: the formulas use ab(a² − b²) with a > b.

Pair (2,3) / (120,169) is labelled k = 15. Under the convention ab(a² − b²) = k m², 2·3·5 = 30 and 120·169·119² = 30·(2·13·119)², so k should be 30 (15 only if areas are halved). The ratio is still a square, so the pair is valid. The parallel pair (1,4) / (240,289) correctly has k = 15.

Entry transcribed '13.24' next to (1,14) with k = 2730 fails: 13·24·407 is not 2730·square, and 13·14 gives squarefree part 546. The pair (13,15) does work (13·15·56 = 4·2730). The digit is overwritten, so the intended reading is probably 13.15; image check needed.

The method gives a sufficient construction (tanφ, tanφ' rational). The page does not show that every fully rational right spherical triangle arises this way; that generality is not justified on the page.
All other table entries check out (verified each).

deep.surprise_reason: The pentagramma mirificum is known to be Gauss's. Also seeking rational instances and reducing the problem to two Pythagorean triangles with areas in square ratio (two points on one congruent-number curve) is a neat Diophantine reduction. It has a clean excess-based parametrization (4φ = spherical excess) and is not, to my knowledge, widely cited as Gauss's. The number-theoretic tools themselves (equal-area triangles, Fermat–Euler doubling) are classical, so this is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major priority claim.
